newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: KLM /Northwest to hike air fares.
newsitem.headline: KLM /Northwest to hike air fares.

text.p: KLM Royal Dutch Airlines said on Wednesday both it and partner Northwest Airlines will introduce a surcharge on worldwide flights from November 1 due to rising fuel costs.

"KLM and partner Northwest airlines have decided to introduce a surcharge...to compensate for the price of jet fuel which has risen by tens of percent since the start of this year," KLM said in a statement.
It said KLM Cargo would also take account of the sharp hike in fuel costs in the tariffs it charged for air freight.

For passenger flights, the surcharge would amount to nine guilders ($5.25) for European one-way flights and 17 guilders for one-way flights to Africa, the Middle East, Pakistan, India, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka and for North Atlantic routes, KLM said.
A surcharge of 23 guilders per single flight will be levied on all other destinations. Return flights were subject to a double surcharge, KLM said.
It said the surcharge would apply to journeys from November 1 this year.
KLM said it would adjust surcharges in line with trends in jet fuel prices.

Last week, British Airways said it was increasing fares on its European routes by an average 2.5 percent, and was weighing increases on intercontinental routes. Germany's Lufthansa said it had no plans to raise fares.
